Meses? (the North-North-East Wind).... In Rhodes it is known as Caunias; for it blows from Caunus, causing ; storms in the harbour of that place. At Olbia, near Magydum in Pamphylia, it is called Idyreus; for it blows from an island called Idyris. Some people identify Boreas and Meses, amongst them the Lyrnatians

english_head:
Some people identify it with Caecias, and also call it Thebanas. .
Eurus (the South-East Wind). This wind is called Scopeleus at Aegae, on the borders of Syria, after the cliff at Rosus. In Cyrene it is known as Carbas after the Carbanians in Phoenicia; wherefore some people call this same wind Phoenicias. Some people identify it with Apeliotes. | Euronotus® (the South-South-East Wind). Some call this wind Eurus, others Amneus.
